codeReview.summary: Feature successfully enabled FULL_DECODE_ONLY HIP graph mode on MI100 (gfx908). The implementation is documented in .factory/library/graph-mode-results.md. No vLLM Python code was changed — this was a configuration/operational feature. The worker correctly identified that TORCH_COMPILE_DISABLE=1 must be kept (to avoid gfx908 torch.compile cluster_dims error), while still enabling HIP graph capture via the compilation-config JSON flag. The launch script /root/benchmark-scripts/launch-graphs.sh is well-structured with proper MI100 environment variables. Benchmark results confirm all three validation assertions pass: server starts without enforce-eager (VAL-GRAPH-001), FULL_DECODE_ONLY graph mode activates in logs (VAL-GRAPH-002), and throughput improvement of +8.7% at c1 and +16.1% at c2 far exceeds the >=95% threshold (VAL-GRAPH-003).

issues.description: The launch script uses 'set -e' but pipes server output with '2>&1 | tee', which masks exit codes. If the server fails to start, the script will exit 0 (tee succeeds). The launch-config-tuned.sh version runs the server in background and uses a health check loop, which is a better pattern. This is cosmetic for the bare graph script since it's the foreground (non-daemonized) version.

The launch-graphs.sh script (unlike launch-config-tuned.sh) runs the server in the foreground (no & backgrounding) and has no health check loop or daemonization. This is inconsistent with launch-config-tuned.sh's approach and could confuse operators. Consider making both scripts consistent in how they daemonize.

A key finding is that HIP graph capture on MI100 takes ~32-34 seconds and adds ~40 seconds to startup (total ~100s vs ~60s for eager). This cold start cost is not documented in architecture.md or environment.md, and is relevant for production deployment decisions (e.g., readiness probe timeout should be >100s). The graph storage overhead (0.16 GiB) is also not documented.

The enable-hip-graphs feature correctly enabled FULL_DECODE_ONLY graph mode on MI100 and produced measurable throughput improvements (+8.7% at c1, +16.1% at c2) with dramatic TPOT reductions (-68-72%). All three validation assertions (VAL-GRAPH-001, VAL-GRAPH-002, VAL-GRAPH-003) are met.
